component.name: Grok Bot
component.summary: Proactive AI desktop agent with a cloud computer

description.p: This is a community package of Grok Bot, maintained independently and unaffiliated with xAI or Anysphere. It repackages the official upstream Linux Debian build unmodified.

Grok Bot is a desktop agent workspace where proactive AI bots work across your connected tools and a hosted cloud computer. Chat, start voice calls or voice notes, schedule recurring routines, and review approvals from a native desktop window.

ul.li: Delegate multi-step tasks to bots running on a hosted cloud computer.
Connect tools such as Slack, Notion, Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar, and custom MCP servers.
Communicate via chat, voice calls, and voice notes with desktop notifications and approval cards.

description.p: An account is required to sign in and use Grok Bot; the desktop app itself is free to install.

Permissions: this package keeps a tight sandbox by default — network, display, GPU, audio (for voice and notifications), desktop notifications, and desktop keyring access (Secret Service or KWallet) for your sign-in. All application state is kept inside the app's own XDG data directory (~/.var/app/ai.x.GrokBot), with no host filesystem access granted by default. Files selected through the file chooser remain accessible through the desktop portal.

Local command execution is optional in Grok Bot. Inside the sandbox, local commands see only the tools shipped in the Freedesktop runtime (such as bash, python3, curl, jq, ssh, and coreutils), not tools installed on your host system. A few optional capabilities are not granted by default; enable the ones you need with "flatpak override":

ul.li: Give local tools access to a specific folder: flatpak override --user --filesystem=~/Projects ai.x.GrokBot
Or grant your entire home directory: flatpak override --user --filesystem=home ai.x.GrokBot
Allow invoking host commands via flatpak-spawn --host (exposes arbitrary host command execution outside the sandbox): flatpak override --user --talk-name=org.freedesktop.Flatpak ai.x.GrokBot
Undo all overrides: flatpak override --user --reset ai.x.GrokBot

description.p: Updates come through Flatpak: this package tracks upstream's official Linux download endpoints, so new releases arrive with flatpak update while the built-in updater stays disabled.
